summary: Thanks come as a run: volunteers, then the campaign team, then family, in that order.
realLife: Five of six winners thank volunteers or the team before family, and give the spouse or parents a personal line.
sources: Mary Sheffield, Detroit mayor, victory night, Nov 4, 2025: https://awpc.cattcenter.iastate.edu/2025/11/12/mayoral-victory-speech-nov-4-2025/
Abigail Spanberger, Virginia governor, victory night, Nov 4, 2025: https://www.rev.com/transcripts/abigail-spanberger-victory-speech
Mikie Sherrill, New Jersey governor, victory night, Nov 4, 2025: https://awpc.cattcenter.iastate.edu/communication/victory-speech-nov-4-2025
Brandon Johnson, Chicago mayor, victory night, Apr 4, 2023: https://www.rev.com/transcripts/brandon-johnson-delivers-victory-speech-after-winning-the-chicago-mayoral-election-transcript
Zohran Mamdani, NYC mayor, victory night, Nov 4, 2025: https://www.rev.com/transcripts/mamdani-victory-speech
Read in full by the local and campaign speeches writer's helper, Nov 24, 2026; every description is a paraphrase.
inGame: people records (household, spouse, children, parents) the speaker already has; campaign staff and volunteers need: a record of who worked on the campaign (door and donor records may stand in)

turns.way: Family is thanked before the campaign team.
turns.pulledBy: a speaker who is warm and family-centered; a spouse in the room
turns.writes: family opens the run of thanks

turns.pulledBy: a small, quick race with no staff
turns.writes: a single thanks, and the speech moves on
